literal: In Huangjian he was made gentleman of the same third rank and general of the martial guard.
idiomatic: In Huangjian he was made gentleman of the same third rank and general of the martial guard.

literal: In the second year of Tiantong he was given an open office, and was also made governor of Zheng.
idiomatic: In the second year of Tiantong he received an open office and was also made governor of Zheng.

literal: In Wuping, for pacifying the bandits of Xin province, he was made director of the guard corps and transferred to fief income of Shangdang commandery dry.
idiomatic: In Wuping, for pacifying the Xin province rebels, he was made director of the guard corps and given fief income from Shangdang commandery dry.

literal: He followed in the pacification of Gao Sihao and was enfeoffed Prince of Yiyang.
idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Gao Sihao and was enfeoffed Prince of Yiyang.

literal: In the seventh year the Later Sovereign visited Jinyang and ordered Shirong, in his existing office, to act as right vice director of the masters of writing and second the Prince of Beiping as northern-palace rearward officer.
idiomatic: In the seventh year the Later Sovereign visited Jinyang and ordered Shirong, retaining his existing rank, to act as right vice director of the masters of writing while seconding the Prince of Beiping as rearward officer of the northern palace.

literal: Soon an edict ordered him and Minister of Personnel Yuan Yuxiu to examine candidates for office within the masters of writing.
idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered him and Minister of Personnel Yuan Yuxiu to examine office candidates in the masters of writing.

literal: He rode a horse to outside the Cloud Dragon Gate and entered the northern gate of the ministry; the censorate impeached him and he was dismissed.
idiomatic: He rode his horse to outside the Cloud Dragon Gate and entered the ministry's north gate; the censorate impeached him and he was dismissed from office.

literal: When the Later Sovereign besieged Pingyang, Shirong was made director of the guard corps.
idiomatic: When the Later Sovereign besieged Pingyang, Shirong was made director of the guard corps.

literal: As Zhou troops were about to enter Ye, he was made grand general of the guard corps and grand tutor of the heir apparent; he fought them off west of the city, was defeated and captured, and was killed by Zhou Wu.
idiomatic: As Zhou troops were about to enter Ye, he was made grand general of the guard corps and grand tutor of the heir apparent. He fought west of the city, was defeated and captured, and Zhou Wu had him killed.

literal: Though Shirong was a fighting man without literary arts, with the court endangered and government in disorder he would sigh to himself.
idiomatic: Though Shirong was a fighting man without literary polish, with the court endangered and government in disorder he would sigh to himself.

literal: Seeing levies without end and gifts beyond measure, he spoke out in lament.
idiomatic: Seeing levies without end and gifts beyond measure, he spoke out in lament.

literal: His son Zizhen, at the end of Wuping, held acting gentleman of the same third rank.
idiomatic: His son Zizhen, at the end of Wuping, held acting gentleman of the same third rank.

literal: Qilian Meng, styled Wuer, was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Qilian Meng, styled Wuer, came from Dai.

literal: His ancestors were of the Ji clan; at the end of the Six States they fled the turmoil beyond the frontier, took refuge on Mount Qilian, and took the mountain as surname; northern speech slurred it, hence the clan name Qilian.
idiomatic: His ancestors were of the Ji clan. At the end of the Six States they fled turmoil beyond the frontier, took refuge on Mount Qilian, and took the mountain as surname; northern speech slurred it, hence the clan name Qilian.

literal: His father Yuancheng was administrator of Yan commandery.
idiomatic: His father Yuancheng was administrator of Yan commandery.

literal: When Buluoji and others rose in revolt on Mount Fufu, Meng was sent to suppress them; he won a great victory and received special rewards.
idiomatic: When Buluoji and others rose in revolt on Mount Fufu, Meng was sent to suppress them, won a great victory, and received special rewards.

literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang he followed Gao Huan toward Heyang and fought the Zhou founder Wen on Mount Mang.
idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxiang he followed Gao Huan toward Heyang and fought the Zhou founder Wen on Mount Mang.

literal: In the second year he was made general who pacifies the east and grand master of palace attendance.
idiomatic: In the second year he was made general who pacifies the east and grand master of palace attendance.

literal: That year he was again transferred to inner and outer office staff commander; for merit at Mount Mang he was enfeoffed Marquis Who Opens the State of Guangxing.
idiomatic: That year he was again made inner and outer office staff commander; for merit at Mount Mang he was enfeoffed Marquis Who Opens the State of Guangxing.

literal: In the fifth year Liang envoys came on a mission; they said they had martial skill and wished to seek out northerners to test against.
idiomatic: In the fifth year Liang envoys came on a mission. They boasted of martial skill and wished to find northerners to test against.

literal: The heir apparent Gao Cheng sent Meng to the guest lodge to receive them; he wore two quivers at his belt and galloped left and right shooting.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng sent Meng to the guest lodge to receive them. Meng wore two quivers at his belt and galloped left and right while shooting.

literal: They also tested strength together in drawing the bow; the Liang men drew two bows, each at three piculs' draw; Meng then took four at once, stacked them, and drew them past the mark.
idiomatic: They also tested strength at the bow. The Liang men drew two bows, each at three piculs' draw. Meng took four at once, stacked them, and drew them past the mark.

literal: The Liang men sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: The Liang envoys sighed in admiration.

literal: That year he was made general who pacifies the army; separately he was enfeoffed Viscount Who Opens the State of Shicheng, with fief income of Pingkou county dry in Sizhou.
idiomatic: That year he was made general who pacifies the army and separately enfeoffed Viscount Who Opens the State of Shicheng, with fief income from Pingkou county dry in Sizhou.

literal: In the first year of Tianbao he was made commander and governor of eastern Qin; separately he was enfeoffed Baron Who Opens the State of Fucheng in Jingzhao commandery of Yong province.
idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao he was made commander and governor of eastern Qin and separately enfeoffed Baron Who Opens the State of Fucheng in Jingzhao commandery of Yong province.

literal: He followed Gao Yang in the campaign against the Khitan and took a great haul of households.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Yang against the Khitan and took a great haul of households.

literal: He also followed Hulu Lüdun on the northern expedition against the Ruru; Lüdun ordered Meng with a light detachment of a hundred horsemen to penetrate deep on reconnaissance.
idiomatic: He also followed Hulu Lüdun on the northern expedition against the Ruru. Lüdun ordered Meng with a light detachment of a hundred horsemen to probe deep on reconnaissance.

literal: Returning to White Pass, he joined the main army and thereby pursued; he broke them utterly.
idiomatic: Returning to White Pass he joined the main army, pursued, and broke them utterly.

literal: He was given three hundred bolts of silk as reward.
idiomatic: He was rewarded with three hundred bolts of silk.

literal: In the seventh year he was made general of the martial guard and gentleman of the same third rank.
idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made general of the martial guard and gentleman of the same third rank.

literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to grand general of the martial guard.
idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to grand general of the martial guard.

literal: Early in Qianming he was given grand general of the cavalry.
idiomatic: Early in Qianming he was given grand general of the cavalry.

literal: In the first year of Huangjian he was enfeoffed Earl Who Opens the State of Shicheng commandery; soon his rank rose to marquis.
idiomatic: In the first year of Huangjian he was enfeoffed Earl Who Opens the State of Shicheng commandery; soon his rank rose to marquis.

literal: In the second year he was made grand general of the left and right guard; he followed Gao Yan in suppressing Xi bandits, won a great victory, and took two thousand horses and thirty thousand head of cattle and sheep.
idiomatic: In the second year he was made grand general of the left and right guard. He followed Gao Yan against Xi bandits, won a great victory, and took two thousand horses and thirty thousand head of cattle and sheep.

literal: In the second year of Heqing he was given an open office.
idiomatic: In the second year of Heqing he received an open office.

literal: When the Turks pressed on Jinyang, an edict ordered Meng with three hundred horsemen to scout the enemy's distance.
idiomatic: When the Turks pressed on Jinyang, an edict ordered Meng with three hundred horsemen to scout how far the enemy had come.

literal: He reached fifteen li north of the city, met the enemy vanguard, and because their numbers were many gradually drew back.
idiomatic: He reached fifteen li north of the city, met the enemy vanguard, and because their numbers were great gradually drew back.

literal: Among the enemy was one fierce general who came out beyond the line to fight.
idiomatic: Among the enemy was one fierce general who rode out beyond the line to fight.

literal: Meng saw him from afar and at once also thrust himself out alone to face him.
idiomatic: Meng saw him from afar and at once thrust himself out alone to face him.

literal: In the space of a bow's motion he stabbed the enemy off his horse and at once beheaded him.
idiomatic: In the space of a bow's motion he stabbed the enemy off his horse and at once beheaded him.

literal: In the third year he was separately enfeoffed Marquis Who Opens the State of Wu'an county and given grand general of the fleet cavalry.
idiomatic: In the third year he was separately enfeoffed Marquis Who Opens the State of Wu'an county and made grand general of the fleet cavalry.

literal: In the first year of Tiantong he was transferred to grand general of the right guard; he then received Gao Zhan's edict to remain constantly at the heir apparent's side and also to know inner and outer confidential affairs.
idiomatic: In the first year of Tiantong he was transferred to grand general of the right guard and received Gao Zhan's edict to remain constantly at the heir apparent's side while also knowing inner and outer confidential affairs.

literal: In the third year he was made central director of the guard corps.
idiomatic: In the third year he was made central director of the guard corps.

literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to director of the guard corps and separately enfeoffed Marquis Who Opens the State of Yining county.
idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to director of the guard corps and separately enfeoffed Marquis Who Opens the State of Yining county.

literal: In the fifth year he was made left vice director of the masters of writing of the joint provinces, the rest as before.
idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made left vice director of the masters of writing of the joint provinces; the rest of his offices remained as before.

literal: He was made chief minister of the masters of writing of the joint provinces and grand general of the guard corps, and enfeoffed Prince of Shanyang.
idiomatic: He was made chief minister of the masters of writing of the joint provinces and grand general of the guard corps, and enfeoffed Prince of Shanyang.

literal: After He Shikai's death Meng gradually took part in court government; on doubtful matters of judgment and appointment all consulted and reported to him.
idiomatic: After He Shikai's death Meng gradually took part in court government; on doubtful matters of judgment and appointment all consulted and reported to him.

literal: Zhao Yanshen, because among fighting generals Meng especially hated treachery and flattery and his counsel was sometimes worth taking, drew him into knowing confidential affairs.
idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen, because among fighting generals Meng especially hated treachery and flattery and his counsel was sometimes worth taking, drew him into confidential affairs.

literal: After Zu Ting had removed Yanshen, he treated Meng as Zhao's partisan and therefore made him governor of Guang.
idiomatic: After Zu Ting had removed Yanshen, he treated Meng as Zhao's partisan and therefore made him governor of Guang.

literal: He had already set out and reached Niulan when suddenly someone reported that on the day He Shikai was killed Meng had also known of it; he was pursued and stopped.
idiomatic: He had already set out and reached Niulan when suddenly someone reported that on the day He Shikai was killed Meng had also known of it; he was pursued and stopped.

literal: He returned, was detained inside the palace, and his household was inventoried.
idiomatic: He returned, was detained inside the palace, and his household was inventoried.

literal: Soon he was released; his princely rank was stripped and he went to his province with only an open office.
idiomatic: Soon he was released, his princely rank was stripped, and he went to his province with only an open office.

literal: In office he was lenient, kind, and clear-minded; officials and people praised him.
idiomatic: In office he was lenient, kind, and clear-minded; officials and people praised him.

literal: Prince Huaiyin Anaigong was old friends with Meng and always wished to draw him up; there was once an edict summoning him to court, as if to entrust him with office.
idiomatic: Prince Huaiyin Anaigong was old friends with Meng and always wished to draw him up. Once an edict summoned him to court, as if to entrust him with office.

literal: Han Changluan and others obstructed it; he was again made governor of Jiao.
idiomatic: Han Changluan and others obstructed it; he was again made governor of Jiao.

literal: Soon he was recalled and ordered to defend southern Yan.
idiomatic: Soon he was recalled and ordered to defend southern Yan.

literal: When the Later Sovereign returned defeated from Pingyang he was again summoned to Ye and made grand general.
idiomatic: When the Later Sovereign returned defeated from Pingyang he was again summoned to Ye and made grand general.

literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou; he died soon after.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered Zhou and died soon after.

literal: Yuan Jing'an was a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.
idiomatic: Yuan Jing'an was a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.

literal: His ancestor Gao Qian was Prince of Chenliu of Wei.
idiomatic: His ancestor Gao Qian was Prince of Chenliu of Wei.

literal: His father Yong, in youth, was a court attendant.
idiomatic: His father Yong had been a court attendant in youth.

literal: From repeated-shot general he was recommended by Yuan Tianmu to Erzhu Rong; he took part in the plot to establish Emperor Xiaozhuang and was given the title Duke of Dai commandery.
idiomatic: From repeated-shot general he was recommended by Yuan Tianmu to Erzhu Rong, took part in the plot to establish Emperor Xiaozhuang, and was given the title Duke of Dai commandery.

literal: He was further made general, grand master of palace attendance, left aide of the mobile office for the second summer and You and three provinces, and with staff of authority received and settled more than four thousand surrendered households.
idiomatic: He was further made general and grand master of palace attendance, left aide of the mobile office for the second summer and You and three provinces, and with staff of authority received and settled more than four thousand surrendered households.

literal: Rong also memorialized to enfeoff Yong as Viscount of Chaona county, fief three hundred households, with staff of authority as governor of southern You and acting general who pacifies the army.
idiomatic: Rong also memorialized to enfeoff Yong as Viscount of Chaona county with a fief of three hundred households, and to give him staff of authority as governor of southern You and acting general who pacifies the army.

literal: Early in Tianping Gao Huan made him left aide of the mobile office; soon he was made governor of Ying, then again governor of northern Yang.
idiomatic: Early in Tianping Gao Huan made him left aide of the mobile office; soon he was made governor of Ying, then again governor of northern Yang.

literal: In Tianbao he was summoned as chief minister of the grand granary, transferred to silver-blue-luminous grandee, and by precedent his title was reduced to Baron of Ganxiang.
idiomatic: In Tianbao he was summoned as chief minister of the grand granary, transferred to silver-blue-luminous grandee, and by precedent his title was reduced to Baron of Ganxiang.

literal: In the second year of Daning he was transferred to gold-purple-luminous grandee.
idiomatic: In the second year of Daning he was transferred to gold-purple-luminous grandee.

literal: Jing'an was deep, keen, and capable; from youth he was skilled at mounted archery and good at serving men.
idiomatic: Jing'an was deep, keen, and capable; from youth he was skilled at mounted archery and good at winning men.

literal: On leaving the crimson he was long-flow aide in Erzhu Rong's grand general's office, given general who pacifies the distant; he was again transferred to long-flow aide in Rong's grand chancellor's office.
idiomatic: On leaving the crimson he was long-flow aide in Erzhu Rong's grand general's office and made general who pacifies the distant; he was again transferred to long-flow aide in Rong's grand chancellor's office.

literal: When Gao Huan pacified Luoyang, Director of the Guard Corps Lou Zhao recommended him to fill the capital-area commandery; his father Yong memorialized to transfer the Duke of Dai commandery to him, and he was given front general and grand master of palace attendance.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan pacified Luoyang, Director of the Guard Corps Lou Zhao recommended him for the capital-area commandery. His father Yong memorialized to transfer the Duke of Dai commandery to him, and he was given front general and grand master of palace attendance.

literal: He followed Emperor Wu on the western entry.
idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu on the western entry.

literal: At the end of Tianping the great army campaigned west; Jing'an surrendered on the field; Gao Huan was pleased and at once appointed him commander.
idiomatic: At the end of Tianping the great army campaigned west. Jing'an surrendered on the field; Gao Huan was pleased and at once appointed him commander.

literal: In Xinghe he was transferred to director of trusted attendants.
idiomatic: In Xinghe he was transferred to director of trusted attendants.

literal: In the battle of Mount Mang he fought fiercely with merit and was given the title Baron of the Capital District of Xihua county; the Duke of Dai commandery remained as before.
idiomatic: At Mount Mang he fought fiercely with merit and was given Baron of the Capital District of Xihua county; the Duke of Dai commandery remained as before.

literal: When Gao Cheng entered court, Jing'an followed him to Ye.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng entered court, Jing'an followed him to Ye.

literal: At that time the south of the Yangzi submitted in good faith and tribute missions followed one another; Jing'an was skilled and practiced at galloping and riding, and by nature had bearing and measure; whenever Liang envoys came he was always ordered with Hulu Guang, Pi Jinghe, and others to receive the guests in mounted archery, and onlookers praised it.
idiomatic: At that time the south of the Yangzi submitted in good faith and tribute missions followed one another. Jing'an was skilled at galloping and riding and by nature had bearing and measure. Whenever Liang envoys came he was always ordered with Hulu Guang, Pi Jinghe, and others to receive them in mounted archery, and onlookers praised it.

literal: When Gao Cheng succeeded to affairs he memorialized to reduce his state fief and distribute it to officers and soldiers; Jing'an was enfeoffed Viscount Who Opens the State of Shibao, fief three hundred households, and given general who pacifies the west.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng succeeded to affairs he memorialized to reduce his state fief and distribute it to officers and soldiers. Jing'an was enfeoffed Viscount Who Opens the State of Shibao with a fief of three hundred households and made general who pacifies the west.

literal: He was also made governor of Tong and given general who guards the west; his son was made earl and the fief increased with the former to six hundred households; the rest as before.
idiomatic: He was also made governor of Tong and given general who guards the west; his son was made earl and the fief increased with the former to six hundred households; the rest remained as before.

literal: Early in Tianbao he was given general who campaigns the west; separately he was enfeoffed Earl Who Opens the State of Xingshi, held the magistracy of Dingxiang, and was granted the surname Gao.
idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he was given general who campaigns the west, separately enfeoffed Earl Who Opens the State of Xingshi, made magistrate of Dingxiang, and granted the surname Gao.

literal: In the third year he followed in the defeat of the Kumo Xi on the Dai River and was transferred to grand commander of the left and right guard; his other offices all remained as before.
idiomatic: In the third year he followed the defeat of the Kumo Xi on the Dai River and was transferred to grand commander of the left and right guard; his other offices all remained as before.

literal: In the fourth year he followed the campaign against the Khitan at Yellow Dragon and held acting administrator of northern Ping.
idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed the campaign against the Khitan at Yellow Dragon and held acting administrator of northern Ping.

literal: Later he repeatedly followed the imperial carriage in again defeating the Ruru; he was transferred to grand general of the martial guard, then again to grand general of the left and right guard, and concurrently minister of the seven armories.
idiomatic: Later he repeatedly followed the imperial carriage in again defeating the Ruru. He was transferred to grand general of the martial guard, then again to grand general of the left and right guard, and concurrently minister of the seven armories.

literal: At that time the long wall was first being built and frontier garrisons were not yet established; the Turks were strong and there was fear they might invade the border; an edict still ordered Jing'an with the various armies to patrol the frontier for defense.
idiomatic: At that time the long wall was first being built and frontier garrisons were not yet established. The Turks were strong and there was fear they might invade the border, so an edict ordered Jing'an with the various armies to patrol the frontier for defense.

literal: Because the command was broad and his troops were rich in goods, bribery soon ran openly.
idiomatic: Because the command was broad and his troops were rich in goods, bribery soon ran openly.

literal: Gao Yang heard of it and sent envoys to investigate; the colleagues on the mission were filthy with graft, but Jing'an had not the slightest offense.
idiomatic: Gao Yang heard of it and sent envoys to investigate. The colleagues on the mission were filthy with graft, but Jing'an had not the slightest offense.

literal: The emperor deeply admired and sighed over this and therefore ordered the relevant office to give him five hundred bolts of the silk gathered as graft, to display his clean conduct.
idiomatic: The emperor deeply admired this and therefore ordered the relevant office to give him five hundred bolts of the silk gathered as graft, to display his clean conduct.

literal: He was again transferred to minister of the ministry of justice, given gentleman of the same third rank and fief income of Gaoping commandery dry, and again made gentleman of the same third rank.
idiomatic: He was again transferred to minister of the ministry of justice, given gentleman of the same third rank and fief income from Gaoping commandery dry, and again made gentleman of the same third rank.

literal: In the first year of Qianming he was transferred to minister of the seven armories and given grand general of the cavalry.
idiomatic: In the first year of Qianming he was transferred to minister of the seven armories and given grand general of the cavalry.

literal: In the first year of Huangjian he was also made attendant within the palace, sent by post horse to Ye to comfort and reward the hundred offices and inspect local customs.
idiomatic: In the first year of Huangjian he was also made attendant within the palace, sent by post horse to Ye to comfort and reward the hundred offices and inspect local customs.

literal: Gao Yan once feasted and shot with the ministers in the western garden; more than two hundred civil and military men took part.
idiomatic: Gao Yan once feasted and shot with the ministers in the western garden; more than two hundred civil and military men took part.

literal: The target was set more than a hundred forty paces from the hall; those who hit the mark were given fine horses and gold, jade, brocade, and the like.
idiomatic: The target was set more than a hundred forty paces from the hall; those who hit the mark were given fine horses and gold, jade, brocade, and the like.

literal: One man shot the beast's head, missing the nose by only a little more than an inch.
idiomatic: One man shot the beast's head, missing the nose by only a little more than an inch.

literal: Only Jing'an still had one arrow unshot; the emperor ordered Jing'an to loose it; Jing'an slowly composed his bearing, drew the bow full, and struck the beast's nose squarely.
idiomatic: Only Jing'an still had one arrow unshot. The emperor ordered him to loose it. Jing'an slowly composed his bearing, drew the bow full, and struck the beast's nose squarely.

literal: The emperor sighed in admiration and praised it; he was specially given two horses, and jade and silks beyond the usual measure.
idiomatic: The emperor sighed in admiration and praised it; he was specially given two horses, and jade and silks beyond the usual measure.

literal: Earlier, Yong's elder brother Zuo had inherited the title Prince of Chenliu; when Zuo died his son Jinghao succeeded.
idiomatic: Earlier, Yong's elder brother Zuo had inherited the title Prince of Chenliu; when Zuo died his son Jinghao succeeded.

literal: In Tianbao many of the Yuan imperial house who were near kin were put to death.
idiomatic: In Tianbao many of the Yuan imperial house who were near kin were put to death.

literal: Distant clansmen such as Jing'an discussed asking for the surname Gao; Jinghao said: "How can one abandon one's own clan and follow another surname? A great man would rather be jade shattered than tile whole!
idiomatic: Distant clansmen such as Jing'an discussed asking for the surname Gao. Jinghao said, "How can one abandon one's own clan and follow another surname? A great man would rather be jade shattered than tile whole!

literal: " Jing'an then reported these words to Gao Yang; Jinghao was therefore seized and executed, and his household was moved to Pengcheng.
idiomatic: " Jing'an then reported these words to Gao Yang. Jinghao was seized and executed, and his household was moved to Pengcheng.

literal: Thereby Jing'an alone was granted the surname Gao; beyond that, others were left to their original surnames.
idiomatic: Thereby Jing'an alone was granted the surname Gao; beyond that, others were left to their original surnames.

literal: Yong's younger brother Zhongzi Yu, styled Jingyu, had fine looks and capacity.
idiomatic: Yong's younger brother Zhongzi Yu, styled Jingyu, had fine looks and capacity.
